english.title: Fail to declare goods obtained in the United Kingdom
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), failed to declare goods, namely **(..SPECIFY..)

(A)_[carried with you]_
(B)_[contained in your baggage]_

which, being dutiable goods or taxable goods, you had obtained in the United Kingdom without payment of duty or tax and for which you were not entitled to exemption from duty or tax by virtue of provision made by regulations under

(C)_[section 19 of the Taxation (Cross-border Trade) Act 2018 relating to any relief conferred on persons entering the United Kindom]_
(D)_[section 13 of the Customs and Excise Duties (General Reliefs) Act 1979]_
english.legislation: Contrary to section 78(1) and (3) of the Customs and Excise Management Act 1979.

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) For the purposes of this section, anything carried by the person means carried by sea, air or train and includes clothing worn by the person.
(ii) THIS IS AN ABSOLUTE OFFENCE - therefore an offence is committed when a person fails to declare goods to which no exemption applies.
(iii) See section 49 for forfeiture provisions.
(iv) For offences committed on or before 30th December 2020 see offence wording document H3678 (CJS code CE79151).

Three times the value of the thing not declared or of a fine of level three on the standard scale, whichever is the greater.
